issues.legal_issue: An execution proceeding is not finally terminated merely because the executing court records it as closed when the court did not intend to end it.
material_facts: Execution of the decree was stayed while appeals by the judgment-debtors were pending.
The executing court recorded the execution petition as closed during the stay, and a later order described it as merely closed and allowed further proceedings from the stage previously reached.
The circumstances showed that the executing court intended to keep the execution petition pending rather than finally dispose of it.
issues.conclusion: The earlier execution petition remained pending; the later application could be used to continue it.
issues.legal_principle: The substance and intended effect of an executing court’s order, considered in its circumstances, govern whether execution proceedings were finally terminated; the terminology used does not control. The Court did not decide whether the Code of Civil Procedure authorized closure for statistical purposes, and held that even an unauthorized order of that kind did not amount to dismissal when the court intended to keep the proceeding pending. It referred to Order XXI, rules 17, 23 and 57 of the Code of Civil Procedure and to Biswa Sonan Chunder Gossyamy v. Binanda Chunder Dibingar Adhikar Gossyamy, Vadlamannati Damodara Rao v. The Official Receiver, Kistna, and Moidin Kutty v. Doraiswami.

rule.if: execution_case and closure_order_made and closure_during_stay and court_did_not_intend_final_termination

predicates.execution_case: The proceeding is an application to execute a decree.
predicates.closure_order_made: The executing court recorded the execution application as closed or used similar terminology.
predicates.closure_during_stay: The executing court recorded the closure while a stay prevented further execution.
predicates.court_did_not_intend_final_termination: The circumstances and the court’s order showed that the court did not intend finally to terminate the execution proceeding.

issues.definition: When an execution application is recorded as closed during a stay and the court did not intend finally to terminate it, the application remains pending.

issues.legal_issue: A later application to continue a pending execution proceeding is not a fresh application when it seeks substantially the same relief against substantially the same parties and properties.
material_facts: The later execution application was filed more than twelve years after the decree, but the earlier execution petition had not been finally disposed of.

The later application sought to continue the earlier execution proceeding and to sell properties already included in the earlier application; it omitted some of those properties but sought no new property.
Any additional parties were legal representatives of deceased parties or a representative of an insolvent party.
A request concerning money deposited in court had been made separately and dismissed.
The later application sought substantially the same relief against substantially the same parties and properties as the earlier application.
issues.conclusion: The later application was not a fresh application within the meaning of section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and the execution could proceed on the basis of the pending earlier application.
issues.legal_principle: Section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure bars an order for execution on a fresh application made after the prescribed period. The amendment replacing “subsequent application” with “fresh application” distinguishes a substantive fresh application from an application to revive or continue one already pending. A later application is fresh if the earlier one was finally disposed of, if it seeks relief against different parties or properties, or if it seeks substantially different relief. The Court relied on and discussed Bandhu Singh v. Kayastha Trading Bank, Sri Raja D. K. Venkata Lingama Nayanim v. Raja Inuganti Rajagopala Venkata Narasimha Rayanim, Ippagunta Lakshminarasinga Rao v. Ippagunta Balasubrahmanyam, and Gajanand Sah v. Dayanand Thakur.

rule.if: execution_case and later_application_followed_long_delay and earlier_execution_pending and substantially_same_parties and same_properties_as_earlier_application and no_substantially_different_relief

predicates.execution_case: The proceeding concerns an application to execute a decree.
predicates.later_application_followed_long_delay: The later execution application was filed after a long interval from the decree.
predicates.earlier_execution_pending: The earlier execution application had not been finally disposed of and remained pending.
predicates.substantially_same_parties: The later application proceeded against substantially the same parties, with any additions being representatives or successors of earlier parties.
predicates.same_properties_as_earlier_application: The later application proceeded only against properties included in the earlier application, even if it omitted some of them.
predicates.no_substantially_different_relief: The later application did not seek relief substantially different from that sought in the earlier application.

issues.definition: A later execution application filed after a long delay is not fresh when the earlier application remains pending and the later application seeks substantially the same relief against substantially the same parties and properties.
